# Lumecon Inc.

> Lumecon is economic impact analysis software: one platform that turns budgets, financial statements, payroll and program records into credible economic impact analyses in minutes, with every result traceable through the data, assumptions and model layers behind it. Built by economists, engineers and researchers with experience at the Federal Reserve and leading universities. Plans start at $500 a year, every plan runs the same model, and the app is free to try (results unlock on a paid plan).

Lumecon replaces the pairing of expensive modeling software plus an expensive consulting engagement with one affordable annual subscription. Every analysis separates direct, indirect and induced effects, carries a full lineage ("Trace this number" on every figure), and exports with its assumptions so a council member, board or federal grant reviewer can verify the result.

## Category

Economic impact analysis software, and an alternative to traditional economic modeling tools such as IMPLAN, RIMS II (Bureau of Economic Analysis) and REMI. What is different about Lumecon: one flat annual subscription (no geography add-ons, no per-project fees); Cedar, an AI economic analyst included in every plan; higher-frequency public indicators supplementing the benchmark datasets on the trusted input-output core; reservations and trust lands as first-class regions; and a lineage behind every result. Lumecon's position: built on decades of economic science, not frozen in it; the modeling is tailored to each organization, the price is not. AI assists inside the workflow while trained economists remain responsible for assumptions, methods and validation. Lumecon is not affiliated with or endorsed by IMPLAN or REMI.

## One platform

There is one Lumecon application. It learns what kind of organization the customer is (city, county, state agency, university, nonprofit, business, economic development organization, Tribal Nation, tribal enterprise, consulting firm) and adapts geographies, workflows, terminology and analysis types. The domains localeconomicimpact.com, tribaleconomicimpact.com and globaleconomicimpact.com are audience-specific entry points into the same application.

## Pricing (public)

Prices include taxes and fees. Multi-year agreements are eligible for preferred pricing, with additional savings for prepaid commitments. An organization that qualifies for more than one program or rate receives the lowest applicable price.

- Sprout: $500/year. One user. Full model, Cedar, every supported U.S. geography, unlimited analysis.
- Sapling: $2,500/year. Up to 10 users. Everything in Sprout plus Team Workspace (shared projects, collaborative analysis, review workflows). Most popular.
- Tree: $7,500/year. Unlimited users in one organization. Everything in Sapling plus Cedar Grove (a persistent organizational data library) and hands-on Cedar calibration.
- Free trial: create an account, bring your documents and build an analysis end to end; full results unlock on any plan.
- Competitive transition offer: organizations already paying for qualifying economic impact analysis or economic modeling software can move to Lumecon for their first year at 50% of their documented prior-12-month spend, up to the standard price of the applicable plan. Minimum plan pricing and other eligibility requirements may apply.
- Consultants: custom commercial licensing for firms running analysis for outside clients, including Cedar calibrated to the firm's workflow. No public price.

## Cedar

Cedar is Lumecon's AI economic analyst, included in every plan and designed into the workflow from the beginning rather than added as a chat layer. It works across intake, analysis, interpretation and reporting: upload PDFs, spreadsheets and CSVs (budgets, financial statements, payroll, program records, prior studies); Cedar identifies the relevant information, maps it into the model, flags gaps for review, assists with interpretation and helps turn results into board-ready reporting. AI assists inside the workflow; economists remain responsible for assumptions, methods and validation. Full detail at https://lumecon.ai/cedar. Cedar Grove (Tree plan) is the organizational data library: Lumecon's analysis-ready datasets combined with approved internal data and reusable organizational context.

## Methodology

Input-output modeling on authoritative public data: U.S. Census (ACS, LODES, QWI, CBP, TIGER/Line), BEA Input-Output Accounts, BLS QCEW, USDA NASS, USAspending, FRED and NOAA, supplemented with higher-frequency public indicators so analyses can better reflect current economic conditions where the data support it. Regionalization, reservation and trust-land construction, data vintages, measure definitions and validation are documented at https://lumecon.ai/methodology

## Capabilities

Cloud (runs in the browser, nothing to install). Security (hosted on AWS, encryption in transit and at rest, isolated accounts). AI native (Cedar is built into intake, analysis and reporting). Analysis types: industry, organization, tribal government, tribal enterprise and Whole Nation analysis (a Tribal Nation's combined economic footprint, statewide and homelands scopes side by side). Historical analysis 2015 to present where the underlying data support it. Exports: workbook (XLSX), CSV tables, printable summary.

## Audience

Governments and mission-driven organizations: cities, counties, state agencies, federal programs, universities and research labs, foundations, nonprofits, businesses, CDFIs, economic development organizations, ports and transit agencies, Tribal Nations and tribal enterprises, and consulting firms serving all of the above.

## Concepts the site covers

Economic impact analysis, input-output modeling, direct effects, indirect effects, induced effects, multipliers, jobs supported, economic output, labor income, GDP contribution, tax impacts, IMPLAN alternative, RIMS II alternative, REMI alternative, tribal economics, reservation economics, AIANNH geography, Whole Nation analysis, economic development, public-sector analytics.

Supported by Cornell's entrepreneurship ecosystem, including the Human Spirit Entrepreneurship Fellows program through Cornell eHub.
